odia: କଳି ନ ଥିଲେ ଦି ମାଇପ କର ଭାତ ନ ସରିଲେ ଦୋଘରା କର
title: An invitation to make trouble
literal_meaning: If you have no quarrel, take two wives; if the rice does not run out, keep two residences.
explanation: The paired invitations offer ways to acquire trouble or use up provisions. Our reading hears irony rather than practical instruction. It also questions the first half’s gendered assumption: conflict is assigned to a marriage arrangement without hearing the people involved. The second half turns to the cost of maintaining two places. Neither household outcome is demonstrated by the saying.
meaning_odia: ଦୁଇଟି ନିମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ ଝଗଡ଼ା ଆଣିବା ବା ଖାଦ୍ୟ ସରାଇବାର ଉପାୟ ରଖେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହା ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ, ବ୍ୟବହାରିକ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ନୁହେଁ। ପ୍ରଥମ ଖଣ୍ଡର ଲିଙ୍ଗଭିତ୍ତିକ ଧାରଣାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଆମେ ପଚାରୁଛୁ—ସମ୍ପୃକ୍ତ ଲୋକଙ୍କ କଥା ନ ଶୁଣି ବିବାହର ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥାରେ ଝଗଡ଼ା ଧରାଯାଉଛି। ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଖଣ୍ଡ ଦୁଇ ସ୍ଥାନ ଚଳାଇବାର ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚକୁ ଆଣେ। କୌଣସି ପରିବାରର ଫଳାଫଳ ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Our reading hears ironic invitations to trouble while questioning the gendered premise.
odia_summary: ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗାତ୍ମକ ନିମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ ସହ ଲିଙ୍ଗଭିତ୍ତିକ ଧାରଣା ପ୍ରତି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: In a discussion of exaggerated advice, a reader quotes the paired invitations. Another notes the extra work of maintaining two places, then asks why the marriage half treats quarrelling as inevitable. This is an invented critical conversation, not household or legal advice.
cultural_context: The source defines two residences. Its marriage language is historical evidence, not a recommendation, claim about women’s nature or account of present law or universal custom.
